title: Dual fixing

blocks.text: A vegetation-management model maximizes $`\sum_j c_j x_j`$ over $`x_j \in \{0, 1\}`$ under rows $`\sum_j a_{r,j}\, x_j \le b_r`$. Some $`c_j`$ are negative: optional overtime shifts cost money and are worth taking only when they let other work in. Write the dual-fixing reduction.

Write `dual_fixings(objective, rows)` in `dual.py`. `objective` maps each variable to $`c_j`$; `rows` maps each row name to a pair `(coefs, rhs)`, where `coefs` maps the row's variables to their $`a_{r,j}`$ (a variable in no row has no entry anywhere). Return a dict of the variables to fix:

x_j = 1 \;\text{ if } c_j \ge 0 \text{ and } a_{r,j} \le 0 \;\; \forall r, \qquad
x_j = 0 \;\text{ if } c_j < 0 \text{ and } a_{r,j} \ge 0 \;\; \forall r

where $`r`$ runs over every row that contains $`x_j`$. This is the lesson's rule, $`c_j \ge 0`$ as in its presolve code: a variable worth exactly 0 whose entries are all $`\le 0`$ is fixed at 1 (funding it costs nothing and loosens its rows, so some optimal plan includes it), and a variable worth 0 with a positive entry is left free. The reference solution tests `c >= 0` for the first case and `c < 0` for the second. Apply the rule once, to the model as given; don't substitute and repeat.

cases.says: a variable with positive value and no row entries is fixed at 1
a variable whose only entry is -1 in a precedence row is fixed at 1 when its value is positive
a variable with negative value and only positive entries is fixed at 0
one positive entry in any row keeps a valuable variable free, even if another of its entries is negative
a variable worth exactly 0 is fixed at 1 when none of its entries is positive, and left free otherwise

origin.section: A Variable That Only Helps Is Set to Its Best Value

concepts: a variable whose increase never hurts the objective or any row is set to its upper bound
